title: QA Plan — Guided Onboarding Checklist (Console) — Feb 2026
content:
Doc intent
This is the QA plan / checklist for Phase 1 Guided Onboarding + “First production launch” checklist in Redwood Console (Hosted API scope). It focuses on:
- browser/device coverage
- auth/API key edge cases
- multi-project behavior
- validator correctness + validation latency (eventual consistency)
- telemetry event correctness (schema, dedupe, privacy)

Owners / where questions go
- QA/E2E: Leila Farouk
- Console FE: Hannah Rivera
- Console backend/state: Chloe Martin / Jada Williams
- Telemetry schema/pipeline: Nadia Rahman / Logan Wright
- Product rollout/flagging: Marissa Cole

What we are shipping (Phase 1)
- Console checklist UI behind feature flag with step state + deep links to docs.
- Server-side checklist state model (per org + project) and APIs.
- Automatic validation for selected steps:
  - API key created
  - “prod mode” API key created/selected (as defined in console)
  - first successful Hosted API request detected
  - first streaming session detected
  - visited usage dashboard
- Emission of onboarding telemetry events (Console + backend) using v1 schema with property allowlist and redaction constraints.

Non-goals for this QA pass
- Dedicated/Private onboarding flows.
- Full automated proof of production readiness (we only validate selected signals).
- Deep SSO/SAML onboarding.

Release gating / acceptance criteria (minimum)
1) No P0/P1 issues in: auth/key creation, checklist persistence, and “first successful request” validator.
2) Telemetry pipeline health: events emitted at expected volumes, no schema violations, no forbidden properties.
3) Feature flag behavior correct: disabled state is truly off (no UI, no events beyond existing baseline), enabled state stable.
4) Cross-browser usable (Chrome + Safari + Firefox latest). Console should not be “broken” on any supported browser.

Environments / accounts
- Staging: preferred for validator testing (we can generate real gateway traffic + inspect logs/metrics).
- Prod: limited verification in beta cohort only (do not spam requests; follow rate limits).

Test accounts required
- New org, no projects (or default project only)
- Org with multiple projects (>= 2)
- Org with existing API keys (both test and prod keys, including revoked/expired)
- Org with limited permissions user (read-only / billing-disabled) — confirm step CTAs and gating

Data setup notes
- We should be able to reset checklist state via admin override (PR-48319) for repeated runs.
- For telemetry validation, we need a way to view events in our internal dashboard / dataset (ENG-23119) + raw event debug tool if available.

Browser / device coverage matrix
Supported for release gating
- Desktop Chrome (latest stable)
- Desktop Safari (latest stable on macOS)
- Desktop Firefox (latest stable)

Nice-to-have (spot check)
- Edge (latest)
- iPad Safari (layout sanity only; checklist not optimized for mobile but should remain navigable)

Checklist UI tests (visual + interaction)
A. Entry points / first-run
- When feature flag OFF:
  - Checklist UI does not render anywhere.
  - No checklist-specific telemetry events emitted.
- When feature flag ON:
  - Checklist renders in the intended location(s) per UX spec.
  - First-run state shows correct empty/intro copy.
  - Step list ordering matches final agreed order.
  - Deep links open correct doc routes (and preserve navigation expectations — opening in same tab vs new tab as designed).

B. Step states
For each step verify:
- Not started → In progress (if applicable) → Complete
- Disabled/unavailable states if user lacks permissions (e.g., can’t create keys)
- Error states (if we render any) are actionable and do not leak sensitive info
- Step completion is sticky across:
  - refresh
  - sign-out/sign-in
  - new browser session

C. Step CTA behavior
- Each step has a CTA that is either:
  - deep link to docs
  - deep link to console section (keys page, usage dashboard)
  - or both
- UTM tags (if present) do not break routing and are consistent across steps.

Checklist state model tests (server persistence)
Core invariants to verify
- State is stored server-side and keyed correctly:
  - org_id
  - project_id (or default project concept)
  - step_id/version
- Updating state for one project does NOT affect another project.
- If the user changes active project in Console, the checklist should reflect that project’s status.

Scenarios
1) Single project org
- Complete steps 1..N in order; verify persistence.

2) Multi-project org
- Project A: complete “API key created” + “first successful request”.
- Switch to Project B: ensure steps are not marked complete until Project B has its own signals.
- Switch back to Project A: status remains correct.

3) Org membership + role changes
- User starts as admin, completes key creation steps.
- Downgrade user to limited role; return to checklist:
  - Completed steps remain completed.
  - CTAs requiring permissions are either hidden or show a permission message.

Auth / API key edge cases
Goals: prevent common onboarding failures (401 due to wrong key; confusion between test vs prod).

Key creation flows
- Create a new test key:
  - Step “Create an API key” completes (if that’s the step definition) OR remains incomplete if step requires prod key specifically.
- Create a new prod key:
  - “Prod mode key” step completes.
- Ensure label “test” vs “prod” shows correctly across UI.

Key usage / 401 scenarios
- Use revoked key → confirm request fails with 401; ensure checklist does NOT incorrectly mark “first successful request”.
- Use key for wrong org/project (if applicable) → request fails; checklist remains incomplete.
- Copy/paste whitespace and header formatting:
  - “Authorization: Bearer <key>” with trailing space
  - wrong header casing (should still work at gateway level if accepted; if not, confirm error messaging)

Token leak prevention
- Verify no API key values appear in:
  - console UI errors
  - telemetry properties
  - network logs captured by our own event payloads

Rate limit / quota edge cases (429)
- Trigger 429 intentionally in staging with burst requests (coordinate with Amara Diallo / Cole Summers if needed).
- Ensure:
  - checklist doesn’t mark success on 429
  - user guidance is correct (link to quotas docs and rate limit handling)
  - retries/backoff recommendation does not cause thundering herd (sanity check docs copy)

Validator tests (automatic completion)
Important: validators are eventually consistent. A core QA output is confirming expected lag bounds and verifying that duplicate/late signals behave.

1) “First successful request” validator
Expected signal
- First 2xx response from Hosted API for a given project (definition per ENG-23113 / PR-48240).

Test cases
- Single successful non-streaming request:
  - Send 1 request (2xx)
  - Observe checklist step transitions to complete
  - Record time from request completion → checklist completion in UI
- Multiple rapid requests:
  - Step completes once; no flapping
- Mixed failures then success:
  - 401 then 429 then 2xx: step completes only after 2xx
- Project isolation:
  - Request on Project A completes A only

Validation latency measurements
- Capture 10 runs in staging (ideally across 2 regions if our staging setup supports this).
- Record:
  - request timestamp (client)
  - gateway log/metric timestamp (if accessible)
  - state update timestamp (backend)
  - UI reflect time (client)
- Proposed pass criteria (tentative; confirm with Dylan/Chloe):
  - p50 < 60s
  - p95 < 5 min
- If outside bounds: document whether UI should show “may take a few minutes” copy.

2) “First streaming session” validator
Expected signal
- First successful streaming response initiation (definition per ENG-23114 / PR-48293).

Test cases
- Happy path streaming:
  - Start stream, receive at least 1 chunk
  - Step completes
- Early disconnect:
  - Start stream then abort connection (simulate tab close or client abort)
  - Step should NOT complete unless definition counts it; clarify with ticket owner (edge case must be deterministic)
- Retry on disconnect:
  - disconnect then restart stream; step completes on successful stream

3) “Visited usage dashboard” validator
Expected signal
- Client-side event when user navigates to usage dashboard (ENG-23115).

Test cases
- Visit once → completes.
- Open in new tab vs same tab.
- With adblockers / privacy extensions (spot check): ensure no hard failure.
- Ensure we are not leaking query params that could contain sensitive info.

4) “API key created” and “Prod mode key” validators
Test cases
- Create key via console UI.
- Ensure step completes for the correct project/org context.
- If key creation happens via API (if supported internally), confirm whether step should complete (align with definition; if not supported, document).

Idempotency / dedupe behavior
- Replaying signals should not re-emit duplicate “step_completed” events with new ids (unless schema allows repeats).
- Refreshing should not generate extra completions.

Telemetry QA (schema correctness + privacy)
Requirements summary
- Must use onboarding telemetry event schema v1.
- Must include required properties; must not include forbidden properties.
- No customer prompt content or model output content.
- Property allowlist enforced; unknown properties dropped.
- Dedupe keys present so retries don’t double count.

Events to validate (minimum)
(Names are placeholders here; verify exact names in schema doc / PR-48255)
- onboarding_checklist_viewed
- onboarding_step_cta_clicked
- onboarding_step_completed
- onboarding_validation_signal_received (if implemented)
- onboarding_checklist_dismissed (if implemented)

For each event, validate:
- event name matches schema
- identity fields present (user_id, org_id, project_id; and session_id if required)
- timestamp present + sane
- step_id present where applicable
- source field present (console/client vs backend)
- dedupe_key present where applicable

Privacy checks
- Confirm absence of:
  - prompt text
  - model output text
  - raw request/response payloads
  - API keys
  - full URLs that could include secrets
- For errors, only include error category codes (e.g., 401/429/timeout) not raw stack traces that might contain user data.

Sampling rules
- Confirm event sampling (if any) matches schema requirements (e.g., do not sample step completions if we need accurate funnel).
- If telemetry is sampled, document the sampling rate and which events are subject to sampling.

Telemetry pipeline correctness
- Events show up in internal dashboards/datasets within acceptable latency.
- Detect missing-region issues (reference INT-3321): sanity check at least 2 regions if possible.

Cohort / feature flag QA
Flag states
- OFF: no checklist UI; checklist events absent.
- ON for allowlisted orgs.
- ON for new orgs (if rule enabled).
- % rollout bucket behavior stable (same org remains in same bucket).

Test cases
- Add org to allowlist → user sees checklist after refresh/sign-in.
- Remove org from allowlist → checklist disappears (confirm whether state persists silently or gets hidden).
- Admin override “reset checklist state” works and is access-controlled (support/admin only).

Multi-session / multi-user behavior
- User A completes a step; User B in same org/project sees step completed after refresh.
- Concurrent actions:
  - User A creates key while User B is on checklist screen.
  - Confirm User B gets updated state after polling/refresh (document expected behavior; push updates not required).

Deep link QA (docs + console)
- All doc links resolve (no 404s), including version-stable URLs.
- Back navigation doesn’t strand users.
- UTM params do not break caching or route guards.

Accessibility + UX quality gates (quick checks)
- Keyboard navigation reaches checklist and step CTAs.
- Focus visible.
- Screen reader labels for step status (at least on one browser).
- Color contrast for step “complete” state.

Performance / resilience
- Checklist should not materially slow Console load.
- Backend state endpoints:
  - return within expected SLO on staging
  - handle errors gracefully (show fallback UI rather than blank page)
- Simulate API failures:
  - state endpoint returns 500 → UI shows recoverable error state
  - telemetry endpoint fails → UI continues to work; telemetry retried or dropped per policy

E2E automation plan (Playwright)
Target automated flows (ENG-23124)
1) Flag ON → checklist renders → create key → step completes
2) Multi-project switch → state is project-scoped
3) First successful request signal (mockable) → step completes and persists
4) Reset checklist state (admin) → returns to initial state

Mocking strategy (to avoid flake)
- Prefer mocking validator signals at the backend boundary where possible (per Slack thread-1738884422).
- If we must rely on real gateway traffic, isolate to a small number of smoke tests and mark them as slower / non-blocking.

Manual QA run list (release-blocking)
- Chrome: full pass through all steps (manual)
- Safari: at least render + key creation + deep links + persistence
- Firefox: at least render + deep links + usage dashboard step + persistence
- Multi-project: manual check project switching + validator isolation
- Telemetry: spot check events in dataset for at least one org and one session

Known risks / watchouts
- Eventual consistency causing user confusion (step doesn’t complete quickly). Mitigation: loading state + “may take a few minutes” copy.
- Streaming validator edge cases (disconnect vs successful chunk). Must align on definition; otherwise QA results will look inconsistent.
- Feature flag regression: checklist hidden but events still emitted (must not happen).
- Privacy regression: accidental inclusion of prompt/model output in telemetry properties.

Open questions (need answers before GA)
1) Exact pass criteria for validator latency (p50/p95) and whether we show UI copy when delayed.
2) Definitive definition of “successful streaming session”: is connection start enough, or must receive >=1 token/chunk?
3) Should key creation via API (not console UI) complete the key-related steps, or do we scope to console-only actions?
4) Telemetry sampling: which events are un-sampled to preserve funnel accuracy?

Signoff checklist
- Product (Marissa/Nikhil): step ordering + copy matches intended onboarding path.
- Eng (Dylan/Chloe): state model + validators match definitions.
- Telemetry (Nadia/Logan): schema compliance + dashboards show expected counts.
- Security (Marcus/Michael): privacy constraints met; retention tags correct.
- QA (Leila): manual run list complete; E2E smoke tests green.
